column3: `orchestrator.sh [options]` is the run entry point (the single driver of the proposer/critic phase loop); it takes only options, no positional arguments.
`-w|--workdir DIR` sets the run/work directory (default `$PWD`); the orchestrator `cd`s into it and canonicalises it to the physical `$PWD`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with stderr `workdir not found: <dir>` when the `-w` directory does not exist.
`-s|--specs FILE` names the spec file explicitly (any name, any location) and bypasses spec discovery.
A relative `-s` path is resolved against the directory the command was launched from (captured before `cd` into the workdir), not against the workdir; an absolute path is kept as is.
`--spec-format FMT` (`native` | `speckit-tasks` | `openspec-change`) forces the spec grammar; default empty = auto-detect; overrides `SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT`.
`--feature SLUG` sets the feature namespace for durable state and selects among several discovered `tasks.md` candidates; overrides `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE`.
`--proposer BACKEND` selects the proposer backend (default `$SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER` or `dsh`); the value is not validated by the flag parser itself.
`--critic BACKEND` selects the critic provider (default `$SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` or `claude`); passed to `critic.py --provider`.
`--max-rejects N` sets the critic REJECTs per phase before halting (default 3); no numeric validation at parse time.
`--max-iter N` sets proposer passes per phase (default 30); passed to `proposer.sh --max-iter`.
`--proposer-timeout SECONDS` sets the global hard wall-clock ceiling of one proposer pass (default 1800).
`--proposer-timeout-phase N=SECONDS` (repeatable) overrides the pass ceiling for phase N only.

`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: <source> must be N=SECONDS with positive integers (got '<spec>')` when a `--proposer-timeout-phase` value or a `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` variable is not `<digits>=<digits greater than 0>`.
`--critic-timeout SECONDS` sets the hard wall-clock limit of one critic call (default 300); passed to `critic.py --timeout`.
`--start-phase N` overrides the derived resume phase; the value is used unvalidated as the first phase to run.
`--verification MODE` accepts `off` | `plan` | `required` (default `required`).
`--test-plan FILE` sets the TEST_PLAN.md projection path (default `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/TEST_PLAN.md` when verification is not `off`).
`--verification-commands FILE` names a JSON document of phase-scoped commands the gates must execute; passed to `verification_plan.py create --verification-commands`.
`--generate-tests DIR` sets the absolute directory for test scaffolds (default `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/generated` when verification is not `off`).
`--telemetry` turns Loki shipping of the event stream on (off by default).
`--loki-url URL` sets the Loki base URL (default `http://localhost:3100`).
`--otel` turns OTLP shipping on (off by default), independent of `--telemetry`.
`--otel-url URL` sets the OTLP/HTTP base URL (default `http://localhost:4318`).
`--live` forces the inline scrolling timeline in this terminal (`LIVE=true`).
`--no-live` forces the raw tee'd output even on a TTY (`LIVE=false`).
`--debug` sets `DEBUG=true`, which adds `--debug` to every `proposer.sh` and `critic.py` invocation (retains raw prompt/response under `<feature-dir>/debug/invocations/`).
`--long-job-phase N` names the phase that owns a long-running detached command.
`--long-job-cmd CMD` is the shell command launched detached (via `bash -c`) before each attempt of the long-job phase.
`-h|--help` prints the usage text to stdout and exits 0 before any state is touched.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 on an unknown argument, after printing `orchestrator.sh: unknown arg: <arg>` and the usage text to stderr.
Every value-taking flag reads its value with `${2:?}`, so a flag given without a value aborts the shell with a bash parameter error (non-zero exit, not the documented exit 3).
The usage text substitutes `@PROPOSER_BACKENDS@` / `@CRITIC_BACKENDS@` with the backend list printed by `lib/backends.py display --role <role>`, so help always reflects the registry.
When `lib/backends.py display` cannot run or prints nothing, help shows `(backend list unavailable: could not run lib/backends.py; see README "Configuration")` and the function still returns 0.
`<install-dir>/.env` (next to `orchestrator.sh`) is sourced with `set -a` when present, as a source of defaults.

Precedence is built-in defaults < `.env` < caller-exported environment < flags: the caller's exported environment is snapshotted with `export -p` before `.env` is sourced and re-asserted afterwards, so a caller-exported variable beats `.env`.
After `.env` is sourced the legacy-name mapping runs a second time, so a `.env` that still uses `WIGGUM_*` names is mapped like the caller environment.
`.env.example` documents the precedence as `built-in defaults < .env < CLI flags` and omits the caller-environment layer that the orchestrator actually applies between `.env` and flags.
`SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` (default empty = auto-detect) forces the spec grammar; overridden by `--spec-format`.
The resolved spec format is exported as `SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` once per run, so the spec shims, `proposer.sh` and `critic.py` all use the same adapter and never re-sniff mid-run.
`SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` (default empty) is the explicit feature slug; overridden by `--feature`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER` sets the proposer backend; built-in default `dsh`.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC` sets the critic backend; built-in default `claude`.

`.env.example` ships `SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC=dsh`, which differs from the orchestrator's built-in default `claude` (and from the comment two lines above it that says the critic stays on `claude`); copying the template changes the critic backend.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` (default 3) is the per-phase attempt limit; overridden by `--max-rejects`.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_ITER` (default 30) is the proposer pass limit per phase attempt; overridden by `--max-iter`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` (default `false`) enables Loki shipping; only the literal `true` enables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL` sets the Loki base URL; built-in default `http://localhost:3100`.
`.env.example` ships `SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL=http://localhost:3110`, which differs from the built-in default port 3100.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` (default `false`) enables OTLP shipping.
`SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` sets the OTLP/HTTP base URL; default `http://localhost:4318`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LIVE` (`auto` | `true` | `false`, default `auto`) controls the inline live timeline; overridden by `--live` / `--no-live`.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT` (default 1800 seconds) is the global per-pass ceiling; overridden by `--proposer-timeout`.
Every set shell variable named `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` is read as a per-phase pass ceiling for phase N (value = positive integer seconds).

The per-phase flag values are applied after the per-phase environment variables into the same map, so `--proposer-timeout-phase` wins over `SPECSTRIDE_PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASE_<N>` for the same phase, and a later repeated flag wins over an earlier one.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_TIMEOUT` (default 300 seconds) is the per-call critic limit, also used for the diagnostician call.
`SPECSTRIDE_CRITIC_MALFORMED_LIMIT` (default 3, `0` disables, no flag) is the number of consecutive MALFORMED verdicts that halts the run.
`SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` (default 0 = unlimited, no flag) is the whole-run wall-clock budget in minutes.
`SPECSTRIDE_GIT_COMMITS` (default `auto`, no flag) enables per-phase git checkpoints; any value other than `auto` disables them.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION` (default `required`) sets the verification mode; overridden by `--verification`.
`SPECSTRIDE_TEST_PLAN` (default empty) sets the TEST_PLAN.md path; overridden by `--test-plan`.
`SPECSTRIDE_VERIFICATION_COMMANDS` (default empty) names the declared-commands JSON document; overridden by `--verification-commands`.
`SPECSTRIDE_GENERATE_TESTS` (default empty) sets the scaffold directory; a non-empty value also upgrades verification `off` to `plan`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_PHASE` (default empty) names the long-job phase; overridden by `--long-job-phase`.
`SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_CMD` (default empty) is the long-job shell command; overridden by `--long-job-cmd`.
The orchestrator exports the unprefixed `LONG_JOB_PHASE` and `LONG_JOB_CMD` so `proposer.sh` can call `ensure_long_job` from its own per-pass loop.
The orchestrator exports `LOCK_FD` (the flock file-descriptor number, empty under the mkdir fallback) so child processes can close their inherited copy before backgrounding a detached job.
`SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID` is an optional inbound distributed-trace id, passed through untouched (never synthesised) and added to every emitted event as `trace_id` when set.

The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS` (the run's events.jsonl path), `SPECSTRIDE_RUN_ID`, `SPECSTRIDE_TASK` (basename of the workdir), `SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` and `SPECSTRIDE_SHIP` (path of `lib/ralph_loki_ship.py`) to proposer and critic.
`SPECSTRIDE_BACKEND_LABEL` has the shape `prop:<proposer-backend>/crit:<critic-backend>` and becomes the `backend` field of every lifecycle event.

The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY`, `SPECSTRIDE_LOKI_URL`, `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_SHIP` (path of `lib/ralph_otel_ship.py`), `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` and `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_URL` with the resolved (flag-applied) values.
The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_FEATURE` (the resolved sanitised slug), `SPECSTRIDE_TRACE_ID` and `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_REJECTS` (the resolved limit) to child processes.
The orchestrator exports `SPECSTRIDE_RUN_START_EPOCH` (run start, epoch seconds) and `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` so `proposer.sh` can enforce the wall-clock budget inside a yield wait.
When running as root (EUID 0) with `IS_SANDBOX` unset or empty, the orchestrator exports `IS_SANDBOX=1` and logs `  note     : root + IS_SANDBOX unset -> auto-set IS_SANDBOX=1`.
`SPECSTRIDE_BANNER_BG` is, when unset and stdout is a TTY, detected once with `lib/theme.py bg` and exported for `banner.py` and the backgrounded presenter.
`SPECSTRIDE_DIAGNOSTICIAN` (default `true`) enables the diagnostician; any value other than `true` disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_ACCELERATOR` (default `true`) enables the accelerator attempt; any value other than `true` disables it.
`SPECSTRIDE_ACCELERATOR_BACKEND` (default empty = the proposer backend) selects the backend used for accelerator passes.
`SPECSTRIDE_OSC_MAX` (default 2) is the oscillation threshold: the run halts when one criterion reappears more than this many times.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES` (default 180000; `0` disables the budget) is the byte budget of the assembled proposer/accelerator prompt applied when appending budgeted blocks.
`SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_PROTECTED_BLOCKS` (comma-separated, default `yield_contract`; set-but-empty protects nothing) lists prompt blocks that are kept even over budget.
`SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING=apply` is the only value under which learned `proposer_timeout` / `yield_poll_interval` decisions are applied at run time (via `learn.py resolve`).
Any non-empty `SPECSTRIDE_LEARNING` value other than `off` turns the learning layer on: tamper bracket, `learn.py observe` and `learn.py evaluate` at phase_done, and the exit summary.
`SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL`, when set at all (set-ness, not value), is treated as an operator override of the yield poll interval with source `override`.
The resolved poll interval is passed to `proposer.sh` as a one-command `SPECSTRIDE_YIELD_POLL=` prefix and is deliberately not exported, so it never reads as an operator override at the next phase.
`SPECSTRIDE_TICK_TASKS` (default `true`) – the literal `false` turns off ticking of task checkboxes after approval.

The `SPECSTRIDE_<BACKEND>_OVERLAY` scope knob is validated at startup by `backend_overlay.py scope <proposer-backend> --quiet`; an invalid value or registry declaration ends the run before any attempt.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `backend_overlay.py scope` returns non-zero (invalid overlay value or declaration); this check runs before spec resolution and before the lock is taken.
The diagnostician call runs `critic.py` with `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE=diagnostician` in its environment.
Each critic call is given `SPECSTRIDE_ROLE=critic` and `SPECSTRIDE_ITERATION=0` as a per-subprocess environment prefix (never exported, so it cannot leak into the next proposer pass).
Each critic call gets `SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_ID=<run-id>-critic-phase-<N>-attempt-<A>` and `SPECSTRIDE_INVOCATION_DIR` pointing at its artifact directory.
`ensure_long_job` exports `SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_LOG` with the long job's log path (or the still-alive prior run's log path) so the proposer prompt can point the agent at it.
The usage text documents that each agent invocation records a capability mode (structured / raw-text / degraded) and that `SPECSTRIDE_AGENT_STREAM=false` forces the raw-text fallback.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: --verification must be off, plan, or required (got: <value>)` on any other mode value (flag or env).
column5: must be off, plan, or required

column3: `orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `--generate-tests` / `SPECSTRIDE_GENERATE_TESTS` is not an absolute path.
Supplying a generate-tests directory while verification is `off` silently upgrades the mode to `plan`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when `--test-plan` is a relative path; the check is skipped entirely when verification is `off`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 1 when it cannot `cd` into the workdir.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 1 with `python3 required on PATH` when `python3` is missing (checked after spec resolution, which itself already calls python3).
Spec resolution step 1: `<workdir>/SPECS.md` wins whenever it exists and `-s` was not given, even when `--feature` is set.
Spec resolution step 2: `.specify/feature.json` is parsed as JSON and its `feature_directory` (relative values resolved against the workdir) yields `<dir>/tasks.md`.
If `feature.json` is unparseable, has no `feature_directory`, or that directory has no `tasks.md`, resolution silently falls through to the glob discovery step instead of failing.
Spec resolution step 3 collects candidates from `<workdir>/specs/*/tasks.md` then `<workdir>/openspec/changes/*/tasks.md`; exactly one candidate is used.
With `--feature`, the first candidate whose parent directory basename equals the raw feature value is selected; the comparison uses the unsanitised value.
When `--feature` matches no candidate the orchestrator prints `spec not found: no feature/change '<feature>' tasks.md under <workdir>` and exits 3 without listing the locations tried.

With several candidates and no `--feature` the orchestrator prints `multiple feature specs found under <workdir> — disambiguate (nothing auto-selected):` followed per candidate by its path and the two `→ specstride run -w … -s …` / `--feature …` forms, then exits 3.
With nothing resolved the orchestrator prints `spec not found: no spec resolved for <workdir> (pass -s FILE — any name/location).` and a `tried:` list of the four locations.
column5: spec not found: no spec resolved for

column3: `orchestrator.sh` exits 3 for every spec-resolution failure (no match, unknown feature, ambiguous candidates).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `spec not found: <path> (pass -s FILE — any name/location)` when the resolved or explicit spec path is not a regular file.
The spec path is canonicalised to an absolute path (physical directory + basename) before it is handed to `proposer.sh`, `critic.py` and `last-run.conf`.
When no format is forced the format is auto-detected once via `specstride_spec.py detect`; if detection fails the orchestrator falls back to `native` instead of failing.

`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: invalid spec (see errors above): <spec>` when `specstride_spec.py validate` fails (zero phases, duplicate or non-contiguous numbers, a phase without criteria).
Every `specstride_spec_*` shim delegates to `lib/specstride_spec.py` and appends `--format $SPECSTRIDE_SPEC_FORMAT` when that variable is non-empty.
`specstride_spec_validate` prints `spec not found: <path>` and returns 1 for a missing file, otherwise prints the phase count on stdout and returns the parser's status.

State-dir resolution: the legacy directory `.wiggum` is used only when `<workdir>/.specstride/` is absent and `<workdir>/.wiggum/` exists; it is never moved or renamed; otherwise `.specstride` is used.
Using the legacy state directory prints one stderr line `specstride: using legacy state dir <wd>/.wiggum (no .specstride/ there; it is not moved)` once per process tree.
`SPECSTRIDE_STATE_NOTICE_SHOWN=1` is exported after the legacy-state-dir notice so child scripts (bash and python) do not repeat it.
An explicit feature value is sanitised to a slug by replacing every character outside `A-Za-z0-9._-` with `-` and stripping leading/trailing `-`; an empty result becomes `default`.
Without an explicit feature the slug comes from `specstride_spec.py feature-slug` (Spec Kit feature or OpenSpec change directory basename), falling back to `default` on failure or empty output.
The run id is `<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<orchestrator pid>`.
All durable per-feature state lives under `<workdir>/<state-dir>/features/<slug>/`.
Unless verification is `off`, the human-readable plan defaults to `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/TEST_PLAN.md`.
Unless verification is `off`, generated test scaffolds default to `<workdir>/testautomation/<slug>/generated`, so `--generate-tests` is always passed to the plan creator in `plan`/`required` mode.
The canonical verification plan is written per run to `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/verification/verification-plan.json`.
The lock is acquired before the run directory, the root symlinks and `last-run.conf` are written, so a launch that loses the lock leaves the live run's log/event pointers and saved config untouched.
The single-run lock file is `<workdir>/<state-dir>/lock`, held with a non-blocking exclusive `flock` on an open file descriptor for the life of the process.
On acquiring the flock the orchestrator writes the owner line `<run-id> <ISO-8601 time>` into the lock file; the file itself is never deleted on exit.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 5 when `flock -n` on the lock file fails.
A lost lock prints `orchestrator.sh: another run holds the lock on <workdir> (<lock path>). Exiting.` to stderr.
column5: another run holds the lock on

column3: Without the `flock` binary the lock is the directory `<state-dir>/lock.d` created with `mkdir`; failure to create it exits 5.
Under the mkdir fallback the owner line `<run-id> <ISO time>` is written to `<state-dir>/lock.d/owner`.

The mkdir-fallback lock is released by an EXIT hook that runs `rmdir lock.d`; because `lock.d/owner` is never removed first, the `rmdir` of the non-empty directory fails silently and the fallback lock stays behind.
End-of-run work (lock-dir release, presenter stop, learning summary) is registered as a chain of EXIT hooks run in registration order, each failure ignored.
At start the orchestrator creates `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/`, `verdicts/`, `attempts/`, `debug/`, `gates/proofs/` and `runs/<run-id>/verification/`.
Migration (3): a flat pre-v2 `<state-dir>/{gates,attempts,verdicts,debug,runs}` tree and `<state-dir>/PROGRESS.md` are moved once into `features/default/`.
When a migration target already exists the target wins: source entries with a name already present in the target are deleted (`rm -rf`), the others are moved.
Migration (1): `GATE*-EVIDENCE.md`, `GATE*-APPROVED` and `GATE*-FEEDBACK.md` at the workdir root are moved to `features/default/gates/` (deleted if already there).
Migration (2): a `PROGRESS.md` under `features/default/gates/` or at the workdir root is moved to `features/default/PROGRESS.md` (deleted if one already exists).
Migration always targets the `default` feature regardless of the current slug, and runs before the resume phase is derived so migrated `GATE<N>-APPROVED` markers are honoured.
Event `gates_migrated` with fields `count` (items moved) and `dir` (the `features/default` directory), emitted only when at least one item was migrated.
Log line `----- migrated <n> stray control item(s) into features/default/ -----`.

At each phase start a stray `PROGRESS.md` in the gates directory or the workdir root is swept to `<feature-dir>/PROGRESS.md`: newest file wins (the stray is deleted if the canonical copy is newer, otherwise it replaces it).
Event `progress_swept` with fields `from` (stray path) and `to` (canonical path).
Log line `----- swept stray PROGRESS.md (<from>) into <to> -----`.
`<run-dir>/run.log` and `<run-dir>/events.jsonl` are created empty (truncated) at start.
`<state-dir>/run.log` is a symlink retargeted (`ln -sfn`) to the relative path `features/<slug>/runs/<run-id>/run.log`.
`<state-dir>/events.jsonl` is a symlink retargeted to the relative path `features/<slug>/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl`.
`<feature-dir>/last-run.conf` is overwritten at every run start with the resolved configuration.
`<state-dir>/last-run.conf` (the active-feature pointer for a bare resume) is overwritten at every run start with the same content.

`last-run.conf` is a sourceable file of `KEY=<%q-escaped value>` lines with two comment header lines; keys: WORKDIR, SPECS, SPEC_FORMAT, FEATURE (the sanitised slug), PROPOSER_BACKEND, CRITIC_BACKEND, MAX_REJECTS, MAX_ITER, PROPOSER_TIMEOUT, PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASES, TELEMETRY, LOKI_URL, OTEL, OTEL_URL, VERIFICATION, TEST_PLAN, GENERATE_TESTS, VERIFICATION_PLAN, VERIFICATION_COMMANDS, LONG_JOB_PHASE, LONG_JOB_CMD, GIT_COMMITS, ORCHESTRATOR.

`PROPOSER_TIMEOUT_PHASES` holds only the operator overrides (flag/env), serialised as numerically sorted space-separated `N=SECONDS`; ceilings declared in the verification-commands document are not included.

`last-run.conf` does not persist CRITIC_TIMEOUT, CRITIC_MALFORMED_LIMIT, MAX_WALL_MIN, START_PHASE, LIVE or DEBUG, and a failed write is ignored; the file is written before spec validation and the verification preflight, so a run that then exits 3 has already replaced the saved config.
`last-run.conf` records `VERIFICATION_PLAN` as this run's plan path and `VERIFICATION_COMMANDS` as the value before it is resolved to an absolute path (resolution happens later, at line 834).
`<state-dir>/stop.flag` is the stop request file; the orchestrator deletes it when it honours it.
`log()` appends to `run.log` only in live mode and tees to stdout and `run.log` otherwise; `term()` always writes to stdout.
`LIVE=auto` resolves to `true` only when stdout is a TTY and `lib/present.py` exists, else `false`.
In live mode one background `present.py --events <events.jsonl> --mode timeline --follow` process renders the timeline; it is killed by an EXIT hook after a 0.6 s grace sleep.
Raw proposer, critic and verification-gate output goes to `run.log` only in live mode, and is tee'd to the terminal and `run.log` otherwise.
At start the banner from `lib/banner.py --phases <count> --states <list>` is printed to the terminal only when stdout is a TTY; a `--plain` copy is always appended to `run.log`.
The rail state list has one letter per phase in spec order: `A` approved (`GATE<n>-APPROVED` exists), `R` rejected (`GATE<n>-FEEDBACK.md` exists, not approved), `C` the phase in flight, `P` pending.
If `lib/banner.py` is missing the fallback title `specstride: from specs to tested code` is printed to stdout and `run.log`.
column5: specstride: from specs to tested code

column3: A plain rail (`banner.py --rail-only --plain`) is appended to `run.log` at each approved phase, each critic-judged rejection, every `run_stop` and at run end.

Start-up record: `specstride orchestrator start <ISO time>` followed by labelled lines `  workdir  :`, `  specs    : <path>  (<n> phases: <numbers>)`, `  feature  : <slug>   (state: <rel>/)`, `  proposer :`, `  critic   :`, `  max-rej  : <n>   max-iter/phase: <n>`, `  timeouts : proposer <s>s  critic <s>s   wall: <m>min`, `  git      :`, `  telemetry:`, `  verify   :`, `  resume   :`, `  run_id   :`, `  stop with: touch <stop.flag>`.

With telemetry off the start-up record says `  telemetry: off (loki export not configured)`; with it on, the line carries the receiver state from `telemetry_delivery.py probe` (configured / reachable / request accepted / query verified).
If the telemetry probe cannot run, the status line falls back to `<sink>: export configured (<url>)`.
The `  resume   :` line reads `phase <N>` (suffixed ` (--start-phase)` when overridden) or `phase <all approved>`.

In live mode the terminal gets a short header: ` feature `, ` agents proposer

, critic `, ` log `.

Unless verification is `off`, `verification_plan.py create --workdir --specs --format --output <TEST_PLAN> --json-output <plan.json>` runs before the loop; `--required` is added only in `required` mode and `--generate-tests <dir>` whenever the directory is set.
A relative verification-commands path is resolved against the launch directory; the document is only consulted when verification is not `off`.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: --verification-commands not found or empty: <path>` when the document is missing or zero bytes.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 with `orchestrator.sh: verification preflight failed (see <run.log>)` when `verification_plan.py create` returns non-zero; its output goes to `run.log` only.

An optional top-level `phaseTimeouts` object (`{"N": SECONDS}`) in the verification-commands document supplies declared per-phase pass ceilings; an unparseable document is silently treated as having none.
`orchestrator.sh` exits 3 when a `phaseTimeouts` entry is not `<digits>` mapped to positive integer seconds.
The wall-clock budget is ignored (never trips) when `SPECSTRIDE_MAX_WALL_MIN` is non-numeric or 0; otherwise it trips when whole elapsed minutes since start are greater than or equal to the limit.
The orchestrator tests `stop.flag` and the wall-clock budget only at the top of each attempt (before the proposer starts), not between proposer and critic.
The resume phase is derived from disk as the first phase lacking `GATE<N>-APPROVED` in the feature's gates directory (no stored counter).
`--start-phase` replaces the derived phase without validation against the spec or the approval markers.

The driver runs `run_phase` for every spec phase numbered at or above the start phase, in spec order, without checking approval markers, so a later phase that already has `GATE<N>-APPROVED` is run again.

Event `run_start` with fields `workdir`, `phases` (count), `feature`, `proposer`, `critic`, `resume` (phase number or `done`), `states` (comma-separated rail letters), `verification` (mode), `verification_plan` (path).
Release verification runs only in `required` mode: `verification_plan.py run --plan <plan.json> --specs <spec> --phase release --evidence-output <run-dir>/verification/release.json`.
Release-gate evidence is written to `<feature-dir>/runs/<run-id>/verification/release.json`.
Log line `----- verification: release gate (fixed argv) -----`.
`run_stop reason=release_verification` with fields `rc` (gate exit status) and `evidence` (release.json path).
`orchestrator.sh` exits 2 when the release verification gate fails, both after the last phase and on the already-all-approved path.
Log lines `# HALT — release verification failed (exit <rc>).` and `#   evidence: <path>`.
Event `verification_release_passed` with field `evidence`.
When every phase is already approved the orchestrator runs release verification, logs the outcome, emits `run_end` and exits 0 without invoking proposer or critic.

The one-line gist of a feedback file is, in order: the first line matching `NOT (MET|VERIFIED|SUBSTANTIATED)` / `is not (met|verified|substantiated)` (case-insensitive), else the first ``- `FAILED …` `` / ``- `ERROR …` `` roster line, else the first non-heading non-blockquote line that is not `The following must be addressed…`; truncated to 160 characters.
The unmet-criteria signature is the sorted unique list of task IDs matching `T<2+ digits><optional lowercase letter>` in the feedback, joined with trailing commas.
For feedback with no task IDs the signature is `text:<sha256>` of the feedback with every `VERDICT <hex>:` line removed, so the per-call nonce does not make identical feedback look new.
The diagnostician runs after a rejection only when enabled, `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exists and its signature differs from the content of `gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>`.
The diagnostician call is `critic.py --workdir --specs --phase --attempt --provider <critic backend> --timeout <critic timeout> --format --feature <slug> --diagnose`; its exit status is ignored.
`gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>` is overwritten with the signature after every diagnostician call, whether or not the call succeeded or wrote a hint.
Event `diagnostician_trigger` with fields `phase`, `attempt`.
Log line `----- diagnostician: phase <N> attempt <M> (unmet set changed) -----`.

The diagnostician also runs after a deterministic verification-gate rejection and on the final attempt before a MAX_REJECTS or oscillation halt; it does not run on the attempt that trips the MALFORMED limit.

An accelerator attempt is due only when enabled, the previous attempt in this run was not an accelerator, `GATE<N>-HINT.md` and `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exist, `.diagnosed-phase<N>` is non-empty and differs from `.accelerated-phase<N>`.

The previous-role memory is local to one `run_phase` call, so after a resume the first attempt may be an accelerator even if the last attempt before the stop was one (subject to the `.accelerated-phase<N>` marker).
`gates/.accelerated-phase<N>` is written with the signature before the accelerator pass starts, so an interrupted accelerator pass is never repeated for the same signature.

The accelerator pass is `proposer.sh` run with `--role accelerator`, the narrowed prompt and the accelerator backend (default the proposer backend); it consumes an attempt number like any other attempt.
The prompt handed to the agent is written to `<feature-dir>/proposer-prompt.phase<N>.txt` or `<feature-dir>/accelerator-prompt.phase<N>.txt`, overwritten at every attempt.

Around an accelerator pass the orchestrator writes `<run-dir>/accelerator/phase<N>-attempt<M>.before` and `.after`: sorted `git diff --numstat HEAD` lines plus untracked files (`<path>\tnew`); empty files outside a git work tree.

After an accelerator pass the orchestrator writes `gates/GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md`: header `# Phase <N> — accelerator pass (attempt <M>)`, the criteria acted on, the list of files that pass changed (lines new in the after-snapshot) and the accelerator's own notes.
An optional agent-written `gates/GATE<N>-ACCELERATOR-NOTE.md` is appended to the acceleration note under `## The accelerator's own notes` and then deleted.
Event `accelerator_start` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `backend`, `criteria` (signature without trailing comma).

Log line `----- accelerator: phase <N> attempt <M>/<MAX_REJECTS> (<backend>) — acting on the hint for <criteria> -----`.

The accelerator prompt includes only heading lines and lines naming an unmet task ID from the phase slice (the whole slice for a prose signature), the feedback, the hint as primary instruction, a footprint rule, the evidence contract, a splice-the-previous-evidence instruction, `This is attempt <M> of <MAX_REJECTS>` and the verification obligations for the unmet IDs only.
The accelerator prompt points at the most recently modified archived `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` under `attempts/phase<N>/*/` as the evidence to copy and splice.

The kind of a critic verdict (`APPROVED` | `REJECTED` | `MALFORMED`) is read back from the last `verdict` event in this run's events.jsonl whose `phase` and `attempt` match, because the critic exit code is 10 for both REJECTED and MALFORMED.
Oscillation detection is skipped unless at least 4 feedback files exist for the phase (archived `attempts/phase<N>/attempt*/` plus the live one), counted before the run-start filter.
Oscillation detection only considers feedback files modified at or after this run's start time, so a resumed run starts a new convergence window.

A criterion oscillates when its ID goes present, absent, present again across the ordered feedback files more than `SPECSTRIDE_OSC_MAX` times (default: 3 reappearances needed); the detector prints `OSCILLATING <criterion> <count>`.
Oscillation detection keys only on `T<2+ digits>[a-z]?` task IDs, so prose-only feedback (native or OpenSpec phases without such IDs) can never trip it.
On an oscillation halt the rejected attempt is archived first, so a later resume cannot resend the unchanged evidence to the critic.
Event `gate_oscillation` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `criterion`, `reappears`.

A rejected attempt is archived to `<feature-dir>/attempts/phase<N>/attempt<M>/`.
If the attempt directory already exists the archive goes to `attempt<M>-<run-id>` instead, never overwriting an earlier run's history.

Archiving moves `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` out of the gates directory (so the proposer's file-existence gate is not satisfied by stale evidence) and copies `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md`, `GATE<N>-HINT.md` and `GATE<N>-ACCELERATION.md`, which stay live in the gates directory.
The newest `verdicts/phase<N>.attempt<M>.*.txt` transcript is copied into the archive as `verdict.txt`.
Event `attempt_archived` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `dir`.

At phase start, if both `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` and `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` are present in the gates directory (left by a halted rejection), the evidence is archived under the attempt label `resume-<run-id>` (directory `attempts/phase<N>/attemptresume-<run-id>/`) before the proposer runs; the feedback stays for the repair prompt.

Both prompts carry an `## Evidence contract` block telling the agent to cite exact workdir-relative file paths, stage line-numbered proof slices under `<gates>/proofs/`, and how the critic's grounding snapshot works (anchored ±15-line excerpts, byte budget, no RPC method names as files).

A budgeted block (currently only `yield_contract`, appended last) is appended only if assembled bytes plus block bytes fit `SPECSTRIDE_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES`; an over-budget protected block is kept, an over-budget unprotected block is dropped; the rest of the prompt is never truncated by the orchestrator.

The yield artifact path told to the agent is `<feature-dir>/yield/phase<N>-attempt<M>-<run-id>.json`.

The proposer prompt tells the agent the workdir, the `PROGRESS.md` path under the feature state directory, the phase title, and to write evidence atomically (`.tmp` then `mv`) to `<state-rel>/gates/GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` only when the phase is truly done.

The criteria heading in the proposer prompt depends on the format: `## OpenSpec tasks to complete …`, `## Tasks to complete …` (speckit-tasks) or `## Acceptance criteria (the phase spec)` (native), followed by the full phase slice.
The proposer prompt (not the accelerator prompt) appends the rendered document-set context block and, unless verification is `off`, the phase's `verification_plan.py slice` block.

When `GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md` exists the proposer prompt adds `## A PRIOR ATTEMPT WAS REJECTED — this is attempt <M> of <MAX_REJECTS>`, the full feedback, one gist line per archived attempt (anti-fixation digest), the hint if present and the acceleration note if present.

A learned value is used only if `learn.py resolve --knob proposer_timeout --phase --default --feature-dir --phase-shape` prints an integer and arm `applied`; the source is then `learned` and the arm `applied`, otherwise sources are `override` / `declared` / `global` with arm `baseline`.

The MALFORMED streak counter is local to one phase in one process: it starts at 0 on every phase and every resume.

The loop bound allows `MAX_REJECTS + 1` iterations but the halt test `attempt >= MAX_REJECTS` ends the run on the MAX_REJECTS-th rejection, so at most `MAX_REJECTS` attempts are made per phase per process.

Log line `----- verification: phase <N> attempt <M> (fixed argv) -----`.
A failing phase gate (non-zero exit) is treated as a rejection with synthetic critic status 10; the LLM critic is not called for that attempt, and the attempt counts toward `MAX_REJECTS`.

On a gate failure the orchestrator itself writes `gates/GATE<N>-FEEDBACK.md`, starting `# Phase <N> deterministic verification gate rejected`, with a `## What actually failed` digest from `verification_failure_digest.py` (or `(failure digest unavailable — read the evidence document below)`) and a `## References` section naming the plan and evidence paths.

Event `verification_passed` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `evidence`.
After a gate failure no new `verdict` event exists for the attempt, so the verdict lookup returns empty: no rail is logged and the MALFORMED streak is reset to 0.

In `plan` and `required` mode the critic is passed `--verification-plan <plan.json>`; in `off` mode no plan is created, no slice is put in the prompt, no gate runs and the critic gets no plan argument.

The prestage step runs `verification_plan.py prestage --plan --specs --phase --attempt` before each attempt in both `plan` and `required` mode; its last output line is the summary, and an empty summary or one starting `No pre-stage commands` produces no log and no event.
Event `prestage_done` with fields `phase`, `attempt`, `rc`, `summary`; a failing prestage never halts the run.
Log line `----- prestage: phase <N> attempt <M> (rc <rc>) — <summary> -----`.

The critic's artifact directory is `<feature-dir>/debug/invocations/<run-id>/critic/phase-<N>/attempt-<A>/iter-0/<invocation-id>/`.

On approval the markers `gates/.diagnosed-phase<N>` and `gates/.accelerated-phase<N>` are deleted; the approved `GATE<N>-EVIDENCE.md` stays in the gates directory.

Log lines `      ticked <n> task checkbox(es) of phase <N> in <spec>` or `      WARN: could not tick phase <N> task checkboxes in <spec> (approval stands)`.

Order after approval: archive leftovers, delete markers, `phase_done`, rail, tick tasks, learning observe, learning evaluate, git checkpoint; ticked checkboxes are therefore part of the checkpoint commit.

Critic exit 3 (config/usage error) maps to orchestrator exit 3.

Any critic exit status other than 0-with-marker and 3 (10, a crash, a timeout status) is handled as a rejection of the attempt.

A MALFORMED attempt below the limit still counts as an ordinary rejected attempt: it emits `reject`, may trigger the diagnostician, is archived and consumes one of the `MAX_REJECTS` attempts.

Every halt goes through `emit_run_stop`: the `run_stop` event is emitted with its key/value fields, then a rail is appended to `run.log` with the phase named by the `phase` field in flight.

Every bash-emitted event is one JSON object per line with `ts` (epoch seconds with nanoseconds), `time` (ISO-8601) and `event`, then `run_id`, `task`, `backend`, `feature`, `trace_id` when their variables are set, then the call's key/value pairs, all values as JSON strings.
Event key/value arguments are consumed in pairs; a trailing key without a value is silently dropped.
JSON escaping of event values escapes backslash, double quote, tab (`\t`) and newline (`\n`) and deletes carriage returns; other control characters are written raw.
Events are appended to the file named by `SPECSTRIDE_EVENTS`; a failed write is ignored and nothing is written when the variable is empty.
When `SPECSTRIDE_TELEMETRY` is `true` each event line is also piped to `$SPECSTRIDE_SHIP event --loki <url> --task --backend --run-id --event --json-stdin`, synchronously and best-effort.
When `SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_ENABLED` is `true` each event line is also piped to `$SPECSTRIDE_OTEL_SHIP event --otel <url> …`, independently of the Loki sink.

Using a legacy variable prints one stderr line per process: `specstride: deprecated WIGGUM_* variables read as SPECSTRIDE_*: <names> (rename them)`; the bash shown-flag is not exported, so each child shell that maps a name prints it again.

A long job is managed only for the phase equal to `LONG_JOB_PHASE` and only when `LONG_JOB_CMD` is non-empty.
Long-job state lives in `<feature-dir>/long-jobs/phase<N>-attempt<M>-<run-id>.{pid,log,done}`, scoped per attempt and per run because attempt numbers restart at 1 in every run.
A long job with a `.done` marker for this run's attempt is never touched or relaunched.
If another run's pid file for the same phase and attempt names a live process, no second instance is launched and `SPECSTRIDE_LONG_JOB_LOG` points at that run's log.

If this run's pid file exists but the process is gone, the job is marked ended (empty `.done` file) and is never auto-restarted within the attempt; a new attempt or a new run launches a fresh instance.

An owned job is started in the given working directory with `setsid nohup`, stdin from `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr truncating the log file, and its pid written to the pid file.

The digest script is hard-wired to one workdir, one feature (`001-ainetops-sonic-evpn-fabric`) and phase 8 (`GATE8-*`); it takes no workdir or feature option and reads the newest run directory by modification time.
The digest is written atomically: to `<output>.tmp`, then moved onto the output path.
The digest script prints `wrote <path> (<n> lines, <n> bytes)` to stdout.

The digest has the fixed sections `# specstride phase-8 digest — <time>`, `## processes`, `## loop`, `## watchdog kills / errors this run`, `## cycles job — section exit codes (last run)` and a static `## known-open defects (do not re-derive)` list.
Digest process lines read `- <script> RUNNING pid=<pid> etime=<elapsed>[ (+<n> stale/other)]` or `- <script> not running` for `orchestrator.sh`, `cycles_runner.sh`, `proposer.sh` and `critic.sh`.
The digest script reads `<state-dir>/proposer.pid` and `<state-dir>/critic.pid` to prefer the pid the loop currently owns.

The digest script depends on the `pass_killed`, `iter_error` and `iter_done` event names and their `iter`, `reason`, `subtype`, `consec` and `evidence` fields, and on `proposer pass <i>/<n>` lines in `run.log`.
